#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-pin-drift.sh — gate (g): architecture pins must not rot (row 90, the
# track-coach lesson: 7 of 17 pins drifted in ONE session, silently; row 541, the
# 2026-08-05 prover pass that found 29 stale pins standing green under this gate;
# row 588, where 48 of the r5 rule-price page's 53 range pins rotted unseen because
# this gate read ARCHITECTURE.md alone — the r5 leg near the bottom of this file
# closed that gap without touching the ARCHITECTURE.md check above it).
#
# A pin looks like `path/to/file:123` (label words) in a node section of
# ARCHITECTURE.md, read through the one node reader guardrails/archformat.py
# (--pins), never by slicing the node body here (SPEC INV-280). The NORMATIVE
# pin is the named thing; the :line is a cache (SPEC E-14).
#
# THE MATCHING RULE (row 541, the prover record's own prescription in F4): a pin is
# proved against its OWN line, by the words that NAME something.
#   * A LINE pin (`file:N`, N > 1) — the label must be carried by line N itself,
#     with a tolerance of ±2 lines, the width of one wrapped sentence and no more:
#     one NAMING word of the label, four characters or more, must stand in that
#     five-line window.
#   * A NAMING word is any label word that is not document furniture. The furniture
#     words — rule, step, gate, line, table, check, node, file, home, section, part,
#     item, row, list, name, page, doc, entry — recur in every window of every
#     rulebook, and matching on them is how the old gate read clean: a pin labelled
#     "rule 20" sitting on rule 19's opening line matched the bare word "rule", and
#     the 2026-08-05 pass found 29 stale pins that way. A furniture word counts only
#     when the label carries no other word of four characters or more ("gates",
#     "the rules"), so a label that names nothing else is still judged by what it has.
#   * A FILE-LEVEL pin (`file:1`) names the file, not a line — line 1 of a script
#     is a shebang and of a JSON file a brace — so its label is proved against the
#     whole file, by the same naming words.
#   * A pin carrying no label at all is proved by the file's existence, and the
#     green line names those pins so the reader sees what went unproved.
#
# Every miss is named — the pin, the label, and what the target line actually
# reads — and every miss is RED. The old gate reported a label miss as advisory
# DRIFT unless --strict was passed, and the push chain passed no --strict, so the
# 29 stale pins crossed a green gate. --strict is now the default; the flag is
# still accepted so an installed host's wiring keeps working.
#
# RED — pinned file missing, :line beyond end of file, or the label not carried.
#
# Usage: check-pin-drift.sh [architecture-file] [--strict]

set -euo pipefail

# the one node reader sits beside this script (both in guardrails/), found by the script's own path so a
# gate run against an ARCHITECTURE.md anywhere (a test fixture in a temp dir) still resolves the reader.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ARCH="${1:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/ARCHITECTURE.md}"
[ "${2:-}" = "--strict" ] && echo "note (pin drift): --strict is the default since row 541; the flag changes nothing."
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$ARCH")" && pwd)"

TOL=2            # the line-pin tolerance, in lines either side of the pinned line
fail=0
checked=0
line_pins=0
file_pins=0
bare_pins=0
bare_names=""
read_files=""

# Document furniture — the words every window of a rulebook holds. Singular forms; a
# trailing "s" is stripped before the comparison.
FURNITURE=" rule step gate line table check node file home section part item row list name page doc entry "

# The label's words of four characters or more, whole and split at hyphens and
# underscores, printed one per line: the naming words first, then the furniture
# words, separated by a line reading `--`.
label_words() {
  local label="$1" w part naming="" furniture="" bare seen=" "
  for w in $label; do
    w="$(printf '%s' "$w" | tr -cd '[:alnum:]_-')"
    for part in "$w" ${w//[-_]/ }; do
      [ ${#part} -lt 4 ] && continue
      bare="$(printf '%s' "$part" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
      case "$seen" in *" $bare "*) continue ;; esac
      seen="$seen$bare "
      bare="${bare%s}"
      case "$FURNITURE" in
        *" $bare "*) furniture="$furniture$part"$'\n' ;;
...
     246 guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh

input.new_string:
PUSH_FULL="${LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL:-}"

# Gate g, pin drift, is the second cost in the local chain: 56 seconds on 2026-08-18, more than
# every other fast gate together. It stays — it holds pins repaired BEFORE a push, and it proved
# sixty-odd re-aimed pins the evening before — but it stops charging a push that cannot have moved
# a pin. A pin lives in ARCHITECTURE.md or in the r5 rule-price page, and points at a file. So a
# diff touching none of: ARCHITECTURE.md, .live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md, skills/ (the r5
# page pins skill rules), or any file an ARCHITECTURE.md pin names, cannot have moved one.
# The diff base is the chain's own, LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE with origin/main as the default, the base
# gate a and the reach classifier already read. Every unreadable answer runs the gate: no base, no
# diff, no pin list. The SERVER runs gate g unconditionally (.github/workflows/gates.yml), so the
# guarantee is unchanged — it just stops being paid for on every push that cannot touch it.
# PIN_REACH_FILES replaces the diff for tests only, the way REACH_FILES does in check-push-reach.sh.
gate_g_can_skip() {
  # exit 0 = this diff cannot have moved a pin, gate g may stand down; 1 = run it.
  local base changed targets f
  [ -n "$PUSH_FULL" ] && return 1
  if [ -n "${PIN_REACH_FILES:-}" ]; then
    changed="$PIN_REACH_FILES"
  else
    base="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-origin/main}"
    git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null || return 1
    changed="$(git diff --name-only "$base"..HEAD || true)"
  fi
  [ -z "$changed" ] && return 1
  targets="$(python3 "$GUARDRAILS/archformat.py" --pins "$REPO_ROOT/ARCHITECTURE.md" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 | sort -u || true)"
  [ -z "$targets" ] && return 1
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -z "$f" ] && continue
    case "$f" in
      ARCHITECTURE.md|.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md|skills/*) return 1 ;;
    esac
    if printf '%s\n' "$targets" | grep -qxF -- "$f"; then
      return 1
    fi
  done <<< "$changed"
  return 0
}

E       AssertionError: '$PUSH_FULL' unexpectedly found in '#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
#
# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

# -- the fast local chain (2026-08-18) --
# The local chain runs the checks that take seconds: the prover record, the pins, skill
# loadability, and the registry and accounting checks. The one slow member is gate b, the whole
# pytest suite, which takes over twenty minutes on this machine and is the SERVER's job — the
# gates workflow runs `python3 -m pytest -q` on every push, in the step named
# "test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)" (.github/workflows/gates.yml). Running
# it a second time on the pusher's machine bought a slower push, not a safer one.
# The old chain is still here and still reachable: LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs gate b locally
# exactly as before, reach-scoped, with its suite-budget arm. That is the flag for a machine with
# no server, a network-less push, or anyone who wants the old behaviour.
# Nothing else moved: every gate whose value is catching something BEFORE the push — gate a's
# fresh prover record above all — runs on every push as it always did.


# Gate g, pin drift, is the second cost in the local chain: 56 seconds on 2026-08-18, more than
# every other fast gate together. It stays — it holds pins repaired BEFORE a push, and it proved
# sixty-odd re-aimed pins the evening before — but it stops charging a push that cannot have moved
# a pin. A pin lives in ARCHITECTURE.md or in the r5 rule-price page, and points at a file. So a
# diff touching none of: ARCHITECTURE.md, .live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md, skills/ (the r5
# page pins skill rules), or any file an ARCHITECTURE.md pin names, cannot have moved one.
# The diff base is the chain's own, LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE with origin/main as the default, the base
# gate a and the reach classifier already read. Every unreadable answer runs the gate: no base, no
# diff, no pin list. The SERVER runs gate g unconditionally (.github/workflows/gates.yml), so the
# guarantee is unchanged — it just stops being paid for on every push that cannot touch it.
# PIN_REACH_FILES replaces the diff for tests only, the way REACH_FILES does in check-push-reach.sh.
gate_g_can_skip() {
  # exit 0 = this diff cannot have moved a pin, gate g may stand down; 1 = run it.
  local base changed targets f
  [ -n "$PUSH_FULL" ] && return 1
  if [ -n "${PIN_REACH_FILES:-}" ]; then
    changed="$PIN_REACH_FILES"
  else
    base="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-origin/main}"
    git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null || return 1
    changed="$(git diff --name-only "$base"..HEAD || true)"
  fi
  [ -z "$changed" ] && return 1
  targets="$(python3 "$GUARDRAILS/archformat.py" --pins "$REPO_ROOT/ARCHITECTURE.md" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 | sort -u || true)"
  [ -z "$targets" ] && return 1
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [ -z "$f" ] && continue
    case "$f" in
      ARCHITECTURE.md|.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md|skills/*) return 1 ;;
    esac
    if printf '%s\n' "$targets" | grep -qxF -- "$f"; then
      return 1
    fi
  done <<< "$changed"
  return 0
}

echo "== live-spec push gate =="

echo ""
echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
set +e
reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
reach_code=$?
set -e
echo "$reach_out"

echo ""
echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
# The reach verdict does not scope this gate (the 2718c69 stand-down, reverted on the owner's
# 2026-08-15 word). A prose-only or scoped diff still sends commits, and the record this gate
# demands is the adversarial read of the pushed RANGE (INV-304) — a thing no file-class verdict
# can stand down for. The only stand-downs that exist are the two PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226.6 names
# by hand: a deletion-only push (handled above, before this chain) and the recordless class.
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."

echo ""
echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"
if gate_g_can_skip; then
  echo "   the diff touches no pin: it changes neither ARCHITECTURE.md, nor the r5 rule-price page,"
  echo "   nor skills/, nor any file a pin names, so nothing in it can have moved a pin. The server"
  echo "   runs gate g on every push (.github/workflows/gates.yml), and LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1 runs it here."
else
  if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-pin-drift.sh"; then
    fail=1
  fi
fi

echo "-- gate f: skill loadability --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-loadability.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate e: prototype fence --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prototype-fence.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-shipped-language.sh"; then
  fail=1

### What runs locally, and what the server runs

The local chain is the fast set. Every gate above runs on a push except gate b, the pytest suite.
Measured on 2026-08-18: the local chain took 144 seconds, and the suite alone takes over twenty
minutes. The server runs that suite on every push, in the `gates.yml` step named
`test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)`. A second local run bought a slower push and
no new protection. Set `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1` to run the old chain, gate b included and
reach-scoped. One thing the fast set gives up: `guardrails/check-suite-budget.sh` rides the suite,
so a push measures the suite's wall-time only under that flag.

### Notes on some of the gates

Gate g, pin drift, is the chain's second cost: 56 to 63 seconds of every push. It stays local, since
pins are repaired because it stands there. It now runs only when the push can move a pin. That means
a diff touching `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md`, `skills/`, the gate's
own two readers, or a file an `ARCHITECTURE.md` pin names. Anything the chain cannot read — no base,
no diff, no pin list — runs the gate. Measured on 2026-08-18: 103 seconds with gate g, 40 without.
The server runs gate g on every push, unconditionally, and so does `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`.

Done. Report:

## E1 — the watchman now judges this project's own sessions

**What changed** (`guardrails/check-worker-restore.py`, `guardrails/README.md`, `tests/test_worker_restore.py`, commit `b4d00f8`)

The criterion came from the transcripts' own structure: every record carries the session's `cwd`. A session belongs to a **neighbour** only when that directory exists on disk *and* `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` beside it answers a shared git directory that is not the gate's own. Every worktree of this repository answers the same shared git dir, so all lane worktrees stay on our side wherever they sit on disk. The reading is fail-safe: an unrecorded cwd, a directory gone by scan time, a directory in no repository — all read as **this** project's and still red.

**Narrowed, not blunted.** Row 598's catch was in tlvphotos — a foreign session. Dropping it silently would have lost a documented live catch, so a neighbour's finding is not discarded: it prints under `ANOTHER PROJECT'S SESSIONS` with session, directory, command and outcome (everything the 2026-08-12 notice was written from) and reds nothing. Row 605's catch (`git checkout -- guardrails/rule-census.json` in our own tree) reds exactly as before.

**Red → green, both directions** (new tests run against the pre-change gate via a plugin pointing `GATE` at `git show HEAD:…`):
- foreign direction — `test_a_neighbouring_projects_session_reds_nothing` and `test_the_neighbours_finding_is_carried_as_a_notice_and_not_lost`: **FAILED on the old gate** (foreign session returned rc 1 with the blocking typed line), **pass now** (rc 0, no typed line, notice present).
- own direction — `test_this_projects_own_session_reds_exactly_as_before`, `test_a_session_directory_gone_by_scan_time_still_reds`, `test_a_session_in_no_repository_at_all_still_reds`: **pass on both** old and new gate, i.e. the catch is unchanged.
- Live effect on the real transcript root (48h window): 10 findings before → **6 ours (still red) + 4 exhibition-engine carried as notices**.
- `tests/test_worker_restore.py`: 102 passed, 1 failed — the pre-existing live-machine test (see below). Every prior assertion kept.

A later commit (`c6ec64a`) makes the two neighbour cases skip inside gate b's meta-run, which copies the tree to a temp dir with no repository beside the gate; there the gate holds no project key and keeps every finding by design (the fail-safe has its own repository-free test).

## E2 — the local chain is the fast set

**Commit `b2ff6e3`** (`guardrails/pre-push`, `guardrails/README.md`, `tests/test_guardrails_unit.py`): gate b (the whole pytest suite) is left to the server. Flag name, following the package's `${LIVE_SPEC_*:-}` convention: **`LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`** — it restores the old arm verbatim, reach-scoped, `SCOPED_TEST_FILES` and all. Gate letters and markers are untouched, so gates u/w (ci-mirror, every-gate-can-fail) still see 29 letters.

**Commit `e442f8c`** (coordinator's addendum): gate g is conditional **locally only** — it runs when the diff touches `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.live-spec/r5-rule-prices-2026-08-11.md`, `skills/`, the gate's own two readers (`check-pin-drift.sh`, `archformat.py`), or any file an `ARCHITECTURE.md` pin names. Diff base is the chain's own `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE`, default `origin/main`; `PIN_REACH_FILES` replaces the list for tests, exactly as `REACH_FILES` does in `check-push-reach.sh`. Every unreadable answer (no base, no diff, no pin list) runs the gate.

**Timings (wall clock, this machine):**
- fast chain, gate g running: **144 s** (a second measurement on a quieter machine: 103 s)
- fast chain, diff touches no pin (gate g stands down): **40 s**
- old chain, `LIVE_SPEC_PUSH_FULL=1`: **1708 s (28 m 28 s)** — its suite ran 26 m 53 s, so the flag demonstrably reaches the old behaviour.

**Server still runs the full suite** — `.github/workflows/gates.yml` lines 38–39: `- name: test suite (gate b, full — the reach map stays local)` / `run: python3 -m pytest -q`. Gate g there is unconditional, lines 52–53: `- name: gate g — pin drift` / `run: guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh`.

**Gate g still catches real drift:** planted a pin re-aim (`skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md:71` → `:471`) in a copy of ARCHITECTURE.md at repo root; `check-pin-drift.sh` exited 1 with `FAIL (pin drift): skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md:471 (rules) — no word of the label stands in lines 469-473`. The probe file was removed.

**Red → green for E2** (new class run against the pre-change `pre-push`): 9 of 11 tests **failed on the old chain**, all pass now; the 2 that pass on both are the server-side invariants (CI runs the full suite; CI's gate g is unconditional).

**What I kept local and why:** gate a (fresh prover record) — its whole value is catching a missing record before the push, and it costs 0.75 s. Every other fast gate stayed. **The one guarantee the split costs:** `guardrails/check-suite-budget.sh` rides inside `check-tests.sh`, so a push no longer measures the suite's wall-time unless the flag is set. It cannot be kept local without running the suite, and CI's gate b step does not run it either. This is stated in `guardrails/README.md` and is worth an owner's ruling in the morning (ROADMAP row 622 already queues that gate's load-sensitivity).
